metadata.title: Corporate Policies and Procedures – Rev 12.7 (For Internal Space Use Only)
metadata.summary: Orbital Synergy Systems' humorous corporate policy outlining office conduct, rocket puns, safety procedures, and data protocols for space engineers.

text:
Orbital Synergy Systems designs, launches, and occasionally lands reusable satellite platforms for a brighter tomorrow—and a slightly busier low-Earth orbit. This document outlines conduct for maintaining both professionalism and gravity (figuratively).

1. Mission Start: Employees should report for duty at T-Minus 0 hours, or earlier if the coffee supply reaches critical depletion. All team members must complete the daily 'Pre-Launch Positivity Checklist,' including the affirmation: 'Failure is just an unscheduled learning event.'

2. Office Conduct: No rocket puns before 9 AM. Laser pointers are to be used strictly for presentations, not dog entertainment. Anyone caught saying 'It’s not rocket science' will be assigned to explain orbital mechanics to HR.

3. Safety Protocols: Hard hats are mandatory in the lab, even during video calls (for consistency). Should a prototype achieve unintended liftoff, notify Facilities before attempting retrieval from the ceiling. Remember: duct tape is not an approved aerospace material… officially.

4. Data and Security: All project data must be stored in the Quantum Drive (Q-Drive) or shouted very quietly into the void. Sharing passwords is prohibited unless it’s with the AI assistant 'HAL-ish,' who already knows them anyway.

5. Employee Wellness: Employees are encouraged to take 'gravity breaks' every 90 minutes to stretch and reorient their orbit. The Wellness Committee’s motto: 'Healthy body, stable trajectory.'

6. Dress code: Business casual. 

Closing Statement: Together, we reach for the stars—but only after filing the correct paperwork and confirming launch clearance from Finance.
